purpose: Dock appearance proposal aligned with the existing camera-pod and winch product language.
evidenceBoundary: Owner selected this appearance direction on 2026-10-14. AI-generated concept imagery remains a style reference, not dimensional CAD, an installation photograph, physical validation or geometry acceptance. Positioning lines are omitted for clarity. Canonical CAD and the rounded-shelter design record govern implemented dimensions and interfaces.

references.role: Compact camera-pod anatomy and nominal proportions reference
Covered winch geometry and removable panel reference
Current warm-white shell, charcoal core and silver hardware conventions
Dock topology, structural attachment and current development boundaries

stages.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ARBI docking industrial-design concept board, for owner review.

Primary request: Extend the established ARBI camera-pod and winch product family into a coordinated high docking station. Create one polished, landscape industrial design board with a large three-quarter docked hero on the left and two smaller useful views on the right. This is a proposed APPEARANCE study, not engineering CAD or a claim of working automatic hardware.

Input images: Image 1 is the owner-selected camera-pod appearance/style reference; Image 2 is the actual compact camera-pod CAD reference and governs the current pod silhouette and proportions; Image 3 is the actual covered winch geometry reference, a black-and-white drawing, whose white removable panel language should be reflected in the dock. Do not copy reference text. Keep the current camera pod recognizable rather than redesigning it into a drone or exposed electronics assembly.

Visual language: warm-white protective shells (#f0f0eb), charcoal structural cores (#1f2426), neutral silver bought hardware (#a8b3ba). Smooth matte molded/printed product finish, broad rounded crown, generous radii, capsule-ended arms, restrained service seams, dark continuous lower rim. Minimal contemporary garden instrument, quietly practical and approachable. Clear white/soft gray studio background, delicate contact shadows, editorial product rendering, refined diffuse light, accurate material separation. No glossy futuristic sci-fi styling or colorful accents.

Physical topology to communicate: a downward-facing dock mounted to an inward-projecting charcoal cantilever arm on the side of a round timber corner post. The dock is high above ground; show only a cropped section of the timber post in the hero. Its axis is roughly 390 mm from the post front face. The stationary protective crown is approximately 300 mm square with rounded corners, substantially wider than the camera pod's 124 x 118 mm warm-white shell and modestly wider than its 230 mm four-arm spider. A gently crowned, removable warm-white outer shelter is the new styling proposal; it sits ABOVE the receiving mechanism and supports no pod load. Keep the arm, guide, locator and retention structure dark. Leave a clear downward-facing flared circular guide mouth under the shelter, broad at its bottom and narrowing upward. Inside the guide is the smaller final locating cartridge and sliding retention fork. Keep sensible access to cartridge, fasteners, drainage and removable roof. Four open line-clearance slots interrupt the appropriate edges so the pod's permanent positioning cables can exit upward/outward toward the four remote corner pulleys; do not seal cables inside a roof or draw vertical hanging cords as the normal installed routing.

Pod mating: use Image 2's rounded white fixed upper shell and integrated tapered charcoal lower moving camera head with the small white optical bezel and dark lens. The four charcoal spider arms have rounded ends. Add the documented charcoal structural bridge around and ABOVE the fixed white pod hood, attached to the four spider arms, with a central upward mushroom stud; it bypasses the cosmetic shell. The stud enters the dock UPWARD from BELOW. The receiving fork retains the mushroom shoulder. The pod hangs below the guide with the camera head and optical aperture visible beneath; there is NO docking pedestal beneath the camera, no landing shelf, and no ground charging pad. The four positioning lines remain attached to the spider ends in all views.

Layout: roughly 60 percent of board is the large mounted docked assembly hero, composed to reveal the white crown, dark guide mouth/rim, dark arm, timber mounting and the recognizable pod underneath. Top-right: the SAME dock seen from a lower angle, with the pod about 80 mm below its seated position, showing the mushroom stud, bridge and funnel relationship; one restrained dark upward arrow communicates final insertion. Bottom-right: a clean enlarged schematic-style local cutaway of the same locator and fork around the mushroom stud, showing the head resting on the fork shoulders and the fork retracting horizontally toward the post for release. The fork must visibly retain the wider head while its open U-slot clears the narrower stem. Keep inset assembly proportions coherent with the hero. Use subtle thin gray dividers. Include a small row of the three material swatches near the lower left, not extra decorative objects.

Text: Use only these short exact captions in clean dark sans serif, with generous whitespace:
Title: "ARBI / HIGH DOCK"
Hero caption: "Parked under shelter"
Top-right caption: "Upward capture"
Bottom-right caption: "Locator + sliding fork"
Swatches: "Warm white" / "Charcoal" / "Silver"
Small footer: "Appearance concept — mechanism and clearances require validation"

Constraints: coherent single design across all views; believable same-family pod and dock; physically intelligible downward funnel / upward stud / lateral fork topology. Proposed rounded shelter can refine appearance but do not invent a validated spring, selected motor or dock sensor. Show all structural retention on the bridge/stud, not on the pod's white housing. Preserve the open camera aperture and four-line attachment story. No propellers, batteries, extra cameras, robotic grasping claws, glowing LEDs, unrelated branding, landscape clutter, certification claims or dimension labels. High-resolution crisp industrial concept artwork.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the edit target: the ARBI / HIGH DOCK concept board. Preserve its composition, camera angles, product styling, rounded warm-white dock crown, charcoal arm and guide, timber post, white background, captions, swatches, lighting and typography. Image 2 is an anatomical reference for the actual compact pod's broad white fixed hood and continuously tapered dark lower camera head; prefer that current silhouette without altering the board layout.

Make one focused correction throughout the board: make the DOCKING CONNECTION mechanically intelligible and consistent between the parked view, approach view and latch cutaway.

Pod structural bridge: in BOTH full pod views add a visible, slender CHARCOAL structural bridge attached by four feet to the fixed charcoal spider arms outside the white hood, rising around the hood and joining above its crown. Four upright legs and a simple four-spoke top structure are enough, keep it visually clean and lightweight, no tall rectangular outer cage. The upward mushroom stud rises from the CENTER OF THIS BRIDGE, separated from the white cosmetic hood by a visible air gap. The stud NEVER attaches to or penetrates the white hood. In the parked hero, the upper stud head is inside the locator but the bridge and its legs are clearly visible below the funnel. In the approach view show the mushroom head fully visible above the bridge and below the empty guide, with the existing upward arrow pointing along the insertion axis. Retain the pod's four capsule-ended arms and camera aperture.

Cable routing: there are exactly FOUR permanent positioning cables, each originating at one of the four POD SPIDER ARM TIPS and continuing diagonally upward/outward toward remote pulleys. The dock itself has NO separate support wires or roof cables. REMOVE the current independent wires drawn from the roof and funnel. In the parked view, where the four pod cables pass near the dock, show them continuing through generously open side notches with a visible clearance gap rather than being tied to the roof. In the approaching view, all four cables start on the lower pod arm tips, remain outside the guide opening and slope up/outward; the empty stationary dock has no wires emerging from it. Thin cables, no ropes attached to the wood near the lower pod.

Cutaway: retain the same local view and caption but show a real horizontally sliding fork plate immediately UNDER the mushroom head. A mushroom is a vertical stem with a wider flat round head. The two horizontal fork prongs bear on the UNDERSIDE OF THE WIDER HEAD on both sides of the narrow stem. The open U-shaped slot wraps around the narrow stem, not the head; it is a U slot IN A HORIZONTAL PLATE, not a vertical front-facing U bracket. The head sits above the plate, its shoulders visibly resting on the plate. Show the fork retracting toward the post as a horizontal release arrow (post is on the left in the main views, use a leftward arrow for release). Keep a narrow outer locating cartridge around the stud, and do not add a motor, spring or electrical components.

Do not add new scene objects, propellers, extra cables, dimension labels, logos or text. This remains an appearance concept. Make the same corrected bridge, pod anatomy and cable topology in the two large assembly views. Keep the material family and all existing legible captions exactly.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the edit target, the ARBI / HIGH DOCK concept board. Image 2 is the camera pod appearance reference. Image 3 is the actual covered winch reference, drawn in black and white; its outer covers should be interpreted as warm white with charcoal lower structure and neutral hardware. Create the final clean STYLING REVIEW version of Image 1.

Preserve the large left mounted docked assembly, its new structural bridge attached outside the pod hood, central mushroom stud, the white removable dock crown, charcoal downward guide and arm, cropped timber post, diffuse studio lighting, materials, layout, typography, and the top-right upward capture assembly. Preserve the title, hero caption, upward capture caption and material swatches.

Make exactly two editorial corrections:
1. OMIT ALL POSITIONING CABLES from the ENTIRE board so this visual focuses on enclosure styling. Remove every thin black diagonal wire from the dock roof, funnel, pod arms, post and background. Render zero wires or cables anywhere. Leave the four capsule-ended pod spider arms and their circular attachment holes plainly visible and empty. Leave the dock's clearance notches visible and empty. Preserve the hardware, bridge legs and mushroom stud. The single restrained upward capture arrow stays.
2. REPLACE the entire bottom-right locator/fork cutaway panel with a small product family comparison panel. Two separate isolated product render thumbnails side-by-side on white: the recognizable white-shell/charcoal-core camera pod from Image 2 on the left, and the compact enclosed horizontal winch from Image 3 on the right. The winch has a long low rounded rectangular protective housing composed of removable warm-white panels, a dark central seam/slot and charcoal base; no exposed stack of motors, no elaborate unrelated robot. Render both in the same soft three-quarter studio style, accurately based on their references. They should communicate the same family palette and rounded protective surfaces as the main dock. Under the two thumbnails use the exact panel caption "One product family". Remove the old cutaway, stud/fork graphic, release arrow and "Locator + sliding fork" caption completely.

Change the small footer to this exact text:
"Appearance concept — lines omitted for clarity — geometry requires validation"

Do not add wires, glowing lights, blue/orange accents, batteries, propellers, antennas, dimension labels or additional text. This is an appearance board, not a CAD drawing. Preserve the overall polished restrained industrial-design composition.
